name: GET /api/leadflow/channels/sms/eligibility - may we text this person, and if not, why?
description:
The SOP §18 eligibility gate, asked BEFORE composing (2a99235e-71ce-430b-921e-8a52823c6cdf#AC1). A rep told after writing a message that it cannot be sent has wasted the effort and learned nothing, so the reason comes back here for the composer to show up front.

A PHONE NUMBER ALONE NEVER GRANTS ELIGIBILITY. Only three bases count - express written consent, an existing relationship, or an inbound request - and possessing a mobile number is not one of them. VERIFIED LIVE: a contact with no recorded basis returned eligible false, reason NO_ELIGIBILITY_BASIS, with the explanation "Holding their phone number is not permission to text them".

THE CHECK ORDER IS THE ORDER A REP NEEDS TO HEAR IT (2a99235e-71ce-430b-921e-8a52823c6cdf#AC2, 2a99235e-71ce-430b-921e-8a52823c6cdf#AC3). Permission first, because no amount of waiting fixes an absent basis; then suppression; then quiet hours, the daily cap and the dedup window, which resolve on their own. Telling somebody "quiet hours" when they never had consent would send them back at 09:00 to be refused again for the real reason.

QUIET HOURS ARE EVALUATED IN THE RECIPIENT LOCAL TIME (2a99235e-71ce-430b-921e-8a52823c6cdf#AC3), from the zone passed with the request. Evaluating them in ours is the bug that texts somebody at 03:00 because it is mid-morning at head office. An unknown zone falls back to the business calendar rather than to "always allowed".

NEVER SILENTLY MARK A TEXT AS SENT (2a99235e-71ce-430b-921e-8a52823c6cdf#AC4). Every ineligible verdict carries a fallback naming the channel and the action - send the approved email and create a call task - and the response states that recording an SMS as sent when none went is forbidden. The failure this prevents is a sequence quietly skipping the SMS step while the timeline shows "sent".

QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: A contact with no recorded basis is ineligible, and the reason names why
The verdict carries a fallback so no SMS is silently recorded as sent
NEGATIVE: no subject_ref, so there is nobody to judge
NEGATIVE: no purpose, so the message cannot be consent-checked
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: purpose is required - an SMS with no stated purpose cannot be consent-checked
errorCases.when: no purpose is given. Consent is granted per purpose, so a message without one cannot be matched against anything.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
